t1.title: slugify() leaves double dashes and trailing dashes
t1.body:
`widgets.textutil.slugify("Hello,  World!")` returns `hello--world-` but should return `hello-world`.

Expected: runs of punctuation/whitespace become a single dash, and there are no leading or trailing dashes (so `"!!!"` gives an empty string). Accented letters should still be folded to ASCII (`Café` -> `cafe`).

t2.title: format_cents shows $0.5 for five cents and garbles negatives
t2.body: `format_cents(5)` returns `$0.5` instead of `$0.05`, and `format_cents(-250)` returns `$-3.50`. The docstring says negatives should look like `-$2.50`. Cents must always be two digits.

t3.title: parse_duration only accepts the XhYm form
t3.body: `parse_duration("2h")` and `parse_duration("45m")` raise ValueError, and seconds (`"90s"`, `"1h2m3s"`) are not supported, although the docstring promises them. Units must appear in h, m, s order, each at most once; anything else (including an empty string) should still raise ValueError. Surrounding whitespace is fine.

t4.title: Inventory.remove lets stock go negative
t4.body:
Removing more units than are in stock silently makes the count negative:

```python
inv = Inventory(); inv.add("a", 3); inv.remove("a", 5)
inv.count("a")  # -2
```

It should raise the existing `InsufficientStock` exception and leave the count unchanged (also for unknown SKUs).

t5.title: read_rows breaks on quoted fields and BOM
t5.body: `widgets.csvio.read_rows` splits on every comma, so a quoted field like `"Smith, John"` is cut in two, escaped quotes (`""`) are not handled, and a UTF-8 BOM at the start ends up in the first header name. Please parse proper CSV (standard library is fine); blank lines should still be skipped.
